Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zulake 0.0.0.9000

  • lake_open() opens a Delta Lake table on local disk at its latest version, at a version or at a timestamp, replaying its log from commit 0 as the Delta protocol prescribes: JSON commits, log compaction files, and the reconciliation of add, remove, metaData, protocol, txn and domainMetadata actions. lake_load() builds another snapshot of the same table, lake_version() gives a snapshot’s version, and lake_is_table() says whether a location holds a table.
  • A table that needs a reader feature zulake does not support (columnMapping in id mode, catalogManaged, typeWidening, variantType, variantShredding, or any feature it does not know) is refused with a zulake_error_unsupported_feature that names the feature, before any data file is read. Its protocol field holds the table’s protocol as lake_protocol() gives it. vacuumProtocolCheck, which asks readers only to acknowledge it, is read, and writer features are never a reason to refuse.
  • Inspection, every function returning a base data frame from the log alone: lake_versions(), lake_history(), lake_metadata(), lake_schema(), lake_partition_columns(), lake_properties(), lake_protocol() and lake_summary() describe the table; lake_files(), lake_partitions(), lake_removed() and lake_count() its files; lake_log(), lake_actions(), lake_changes(), lake_transactions(), lake_domains() and lake_checkpoints() the log itself. A snapshot prints a short summary.
  • lake_files(filter =) and lake_partitions(filter =) keep the files a filter on partition columns can match; an expression outside the pruning subset is a zulake_error_filter.
  • lake_count() is NA, with a zulake_warning_count_unknown warning, when a live file has no numRecords statistic, never a partial sum.
  • 64-bit values from the log are doubles exact up to 2^53 - 1 and a zulake_error_int64 beyond, or exact bit64::integer64 values with int64 = "integer64"; decimal statistics are kept as their JSON text.
  • Every error is a classed condition inheriting from zulake_error; a corrupt log (a commit that is not JSON, a partition value of the wrong type) is a zulake_error_corrupt_log.
  • Checkpoints: replay starts from the latest whole checkpoint at or before the version, classic, multi-part or V2 (in JSON or Parquet, with its sidecars), read through qio (now >= 0.1.2.9000, which reads nested Parquet), so tables whose early commits were cleaned up open. A stale _last_checkpoint changes nothing; one naming a checkpoint the log does not hold whole is a zulake_error_corrupt_log. A checkpoint that cannot be read is passed over for an earlier one or the commits; zulake_error_checkpoint_unreadable is left for a version that needs it when commit 0 is gone. A version older than the earliest checkpoint whose commits were removed is a zulake_error_version. Statistics come from the stats JSON, as in a commit; stats_parsed is not read.
  • lake_read() returns a snapshot’s rows and lake_walk() calls a function on each file’s rows, reading the data files with qio (now imported) and adding partition columns from the log. A filter prunes files by partition values and statistics (minimum, maximum, null and record counts) before any is read, then filters rows. Comparisons in the subset are exact: long, integer and decimal columns digit by digit (a double with no exact 15-digit form is a zulake_error_filter asking for the value as text), strings in UTF-8 byte order whatever the collation. lake_files(filter =) and lake_partitions(filter =) now use the statistics too.
  • Columns qio cannot return (nested columns, and decimals of precision above 15, which a double cannot hold) are left out of a read with a zulake_warning_column_skipped warning naming each, or are a zulake_error_column_unreadable error when named in columns or used in filter. A decimal of precision 15 or less is a double.
  • Deletion vectors: lake_read() and lake_walk() never return the rows a deletion vector marks, inline (Z85) or in a file at a relative or absolute path, with each vector’s CRC-32 checked. lake_deletion_vectors() lists each live file’s descriptor and, with rows = TRUE, the 0-based positions of its deleted rows. The rows need the suggested zuroar package (installed with pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuroar")); without it such a read is a zulake_error_missing_package naming it, while lake_count() and lake_deletion_vectors(rows = FALSE) still work. A vector that does not agree with its descriptor (checksum, magic number, size, row count) is a zulake_error_corrupt_log, and no rows are returned.
  • Tables with column mapping in name mode are read, by physical column names in the files and logical names in the result; timestamp_ntz columns are POSIXct in UTC.
  • lake_count(footers = TRUE) reads the row count of each file without a numRecords statistic from its Parquet footer.
  • A long statistic in lake_files() that the int64 mode cannot hold (such as -2^63) is now NA with a zulake_warning_int64 warning, once per column, instead of an error; its digits stay in action.
  • A filter is now row-wise by construction. Besides the pruning subset it may apply a fixed list of row-wise functions to columns (arithmetic, abs(), round(), nchar(), substr(), grepl(), xor(), as.numeric() and others, listed in ?lake_read) and compare two columns; these filter rows after reading and never prune, and lake_files() and lake_partitions() refuse them. Any other call with a column inside it (max(x), mean(x), rank(x), duplicated(x), %in% with a column on the right, a function of your own) is a zulake_error_filter in every function, so a filter’s rows never depend on how the table is split into files. The functions are base R’s, whatever the caller defines.
  • Fixed: on Windows, time travel by timestamp could open the version before a commit whose file time is a whole millisecond, at exactly that millisecond, because R reads Windows file times up to about 1 µs low. File times are now rounded to 10 µs before they are truncated to milliseconds.
  • Tables on Azure: every function now reads a table given as abfss://<container>@<account>.dfs.core.windows.net/<path>, https://<account>.dfs.core.windows.net/<container>/<path> or https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<path>, through the Blob service API, which serves Blob Storage and Data Lake Storage Gen2 alike. credentials is a function returning a bearer token; it is called before the first request and once more after a 401, and the token is never kept in the snapshot, printed or put in an error. A refused token is a zulake_error_auth, other Azure failures a zulake_error_storage with the HTTP status and Azure’s error code. Other schemes, and an Azure URI with a query string such as a SAS, are a zulake_error_uri. Requests go through zuhttp, now imported.
  • The package ships a small example table, orders partitioned by region in five versions, at system.file("extdata", "orders", package = "zulake"). The README, the Get started vignette (vignette("zulake")), now evaluated, and every help page’s examples run on it.
